values.value: How much of your workflow logic depends on re-enrolment, goal criteria, or loops — as opposed to a straight sequence of branches and delays?

[{"value":1,"label":"Re-enrolment is on across most workflows, goals drive exits, and at least one workflow loops. The logic IS the re-entry behaviour."},{"value":2,"label":"Several workflows re-enrol or use goal criteria; removing them would change what the programme does."},{"value":3,"label":"Mostly linear branch-and-delay logic; re-enrolment is on in a handful of places and is not load-bearing."},{"value":4,"label":"Linear, single-entry flows throughout. No goals, no loops, no re-enrolment anywhere."}]
Ask them to open one workflow and read out its enrolment settings — 're-enrol contacts' and 'goal' are checkboxes, so this is a factual answer, not an impression.
If you are not sure, open one of your busier workflows: 're-enrol contacts' and 'goal' are checkboxes in its settings.

skills/mce-mcn-helper/references/framework-reference.md — "Journey Builder -> Campaign Flow ... No 'No Re-entry' equivalent yet - workaround is a DMO tracking flow entry used as segment exclusion", i.e. even the RE-ENTRY SUPPRESSION side has no native element; docs/specs/tier-2/sfmc-next-target-adapter.md — capabilities.flow_control.loops status unsupported ("Flow does not support loopbacks"). Goal criteria have no counterpart in either document, which is the point: three of HubSpot's four most-used workflow features are things the target expresses as something else or not at all. Recalibrated, not reworded: a 4 here requires their absence.
